answerFreeze.reason: Triangle ABC has A=80°; AD bisects angle A so DAC=40°. In triangle ADC, angle ADC=180°−40°−70°=70°.
Hexagon interior-angle sum is 720°. The exterior angles 48° and 53° give adjacent interior angles 132° and 127°. Thus x=720°−(132°+111°+127°+112°+108°)=130°.

Equal minor arcs AB, CD, DE imply equal chords AB=DE, central angle COE is twice AOB, and sector COE area is twice sector AOB. The chord CE of doubled central angle is not generally twice AB; the triangle area ratio is not generally 2 (it depends on the central angle).
